one:
Katrina Joy M. Abriol-Santos is a thesis adviser with five theses recorded in this repository, all of which were advised in 2026. Their research supervision focuses heavily on information systems, which appears in four of their five advised works. Other research sub-topics they have supervised include governance and public policy, which appears in three items, agriculture and food, which appears in two items, management and leadership, which appears in one item, environment and sustainability, which appears in one item, and public health and COVID-19, which appears in one item.

In 2026, Katrina Joy M. Abriol-Santos advised a thesis titled "Sponsor Management and Letter of Guarantee (LoG) Coverage Integration System for International School Manila (ISM)." This work focuses on information systems, governance and public policy, and management and leadership. The project addresses operational challenges at International School Manila (ISM) regarding sponsorship billing and Letter of Guarantee (LoG) coverage caused by fragmented data across four separate systems: PowerSchool, the Student Charging Portal, NetSuite, and the Online Billing.

They also advised the thesis "Verifiable Academic Records for ISM (VERACISM) : A Permanent, Decentralized, Blockchain-Backed Storage for Immutable Reports" in 2026. This research covers information systems and governance and public policy. The work addresses data integrity and authenticity issues regarding academic reporting at International School Manila (ISM), specifically noting that centralized systems lack cryptographic bindings between reports and metadata.

Katrina Joy M. Abriol-Santos supervised the thesis "CADENCE: An AI-Powered Operations Platform for Greenrock Agrifarms SG Trading Inc." in 2026. This project involves information systems, environment and sustainability, and agriculture and food. The research addresses how GreenRock Agrifarms SG Trading Inc. currently utilizes a manual, file-based system to track sales and inventory within poultry operations, which requires significant time for report preparation and introduces high risk.

Furthermore, they advised the thesis "Community Nutrition Information System of Barangay San Andres, Cainta, Rizal" in 2026. This work covers information systems, governance and public policy, and public health and COVID-19. The project involves a progressive web application (PWA) designed to modernize child nutritional record management in Barangay San Andres, Cainta, Rizal, to address inefficiencies.

Finally, they advised the thesis "Digital Farmers' Produce System: A Cloud-based Platform for Optimizing Crop Management and Market Linkages" in 2026. This research focuses on agriculture and food. The project is a cloud-based web application designed to optimize crop management and market linkages in Sinacaban, Misamis Occidental, to address challenges faced by smallholder farmers, such as limited access to real-time information. Evidence of their research contributions is limited to these five supervised theses from 2026.
